element: Safety content in any free text of the case gets its own SE claim, whatever else the ticket contains
source: RYDE-15395890865561 (Ryde Code of Conduct, driver article edited 2026-04-10), item 5: 'We have a zero-tolerance approach to any form of misconduct or inappropriate behavior between drivers and passengers.'; IND-BENCHMARK-NOTES (research note 02: Lyft, Grab and DiDi handle safety incidents separately)
note: The conduct norm is Ryde's (A); handling it as a separate claim whatever the ticket says is other platforms' practice (C).

element: The SE claim is decided by a human
source: AUTH-03 (GOV-IMDA-AGENTIC: 'Organisations should define significant checkpoints or action boundaries that require human approval, especially before sensitive actions are executed.')
note: Same norm as AUTH-03 (B); industry practice (C) agrees.

element: What counts as safety content: a definition read for meaning, with examples; unclear text counts as safety content; rudeness alone is feedback
source: FAIRRYDE (the definition by meaning, the examples Ryde does not name, the rule for unclear text and the line between rudeness and safety)

element: Severity S0 or S1
source: FAIRRYDE (FairRyde's severity scale in taxonomy.yaml)

element: Most examples of safety content: assault, sexual harassment, kidnapping, threats, abuse of any kind, personal questions and comments on appearance, reckless driving, alcohol and drugs, crimes, comments on race, ethnicity, national origin, disability, etc
source: RYDE-15395890865561 (Ryde Code of Conduct) items 5 to 8: 'Assault, harassment, or abuse of any kind will not be tolerated.', 'Do not commit crimes.', 'Reckless or dangerous driving that endangers passengers, pedestrians, or other road users is strictly prohibited.', 'Alcohol, drugs, and weapons are not tolerated.'; RYDE-33362721809049: 'Comments on race, ethnicity, national origin, disability, etc'
note: A4 (FX6 and check rounds 1 and 2): the examples quoted from Ryde, in Ryde's words; religion and other grounds read into 'etc' are in the FAIRRYDE row above.

element: Ryde profile only (organizer cases use driver_wait_start, CW-F02)
source: META-01 (profile choice)
note: Scope pointer: which profile the rule serves, not part of its norm.

element: For an ADVANCE booking with an early driver, the wait starts at the later of the arrival and scheduled_time
source: IND-GRAB-ADVANCE: 'Your driver will arrive early and wait for you for up to 15 minutes starting from the indicated pickup time.'; IND-BOLT-SCHEDULED: 'The scheduled wait time of 5 minutes will be counted only from the scheduled start of the ride.'
note: Ryde's rider policy is silent on early drivers; FairRyde fills the gap with other platforms' published practice, which is what C means. Not a FairRyde extension of a Ryde condition.

element: The conflict with Ryde's older driver text (it counts from the arrival) is recorded
source: RYDE-23575142762393 (driver article, 2023-10-02): 'You arrived at the pickup location and the customer was not present within 3 minutes of your arrival.'
note: Documents the conflict; the rule does not rest on it. A4 (FX9) added the 2024 driver pages RYDE-20244064619161 and RYDE-33362932998937, which also count from 'I'm Here', to the note.

element: The fee requires the driver to be at the pick-up location according to GPS
source: RYDE-4407754403353 (rider article, edited 2026-02-26): 'Is at the pick-up location according to GPS data'
note: Reading it as covering the S$6.61 no-show fee is the META-04 resolution of the fee-name conflict, an interpretation, so B (as in v0.1).

element: ... during the waiting the fee pays for: from the confirmed wait start until the threshold is reached, or the cancellation or boarding if earlier; leaving after the threshold does not count
source: RYDE-4407754403353 (2026-02-26): 'Is at the pick-up location according to GPS data' AND 'Has waited for more than 3 mins'; RYDE-23534478435353 (main policy page, edited 2026-02-26): 'The driver presses "I'm Here", waits for > 3 minutes for the rider to arrive at the pick-up point and cancels the trip (Rider NO SHOW and no trip completion)'
note: Reading the article's two joined conditions as presence for the wait, ending where the main page's 'waits for > 3 minutes ... and cancels' ends, interprets Ryde text (B). Check round 2 (GRD-01): 'at the pick-up point' in the main page belongs to the rider, not to where the driver waits.

element: Pings sorted by time; outside stretches after the driver is first seen inside; GPS outliers (shorter than LEFT_MIN_OUTSIDE_S and followed by an inside ping) set aside; a stretch with no later inside ping is never an outlier on duration
source: FAIRRYDE (open item D24)
note: Moved to CW-F04B (FairRyde's presence logic, D).

element: Data errors: a stretch implying more than SPEED_MAX_KMH is set aside and flagged GPS_DATA_ERROR (DQ-02, gate G1)
source: FAIRRYDE (open item D24)
note: Moved to CW-F04B.

element: The approach: pings before the driver is first seen inside are never outliers on duration
source: FAIRRYDE (open item D24)
note: Moved to CW-F04B.

element: Window edges: outside pings within TS_TOLERANCE_S of the window end (and of the start, for the approach) do not count as leaving
source: FAIRRYDE (open item D24)
note: Moved to CW-F04B.

element: The values LEFT, SPARSE (a gap longer than PING_MAX_GAP_S), CONSISTENT and UNKNOWN (no window, no ping in it, or no confirmed arrival and no inside ping)
source: FAIRRYDE (open items D18, D24, D26)
note: Moved to CW-F04B. Ryde states the condition, not how pings settle it.

element: GPS_AMBIGUOUS when the pings cannot settle whether the driver left
source: FAIRRYDE (AUTH-02 trigger 11)
note: Moved to CW-F04B.

element: Parameters ARRIVAL_GEOFENCE_M, PING_MAX_GAP_S, LEFT_MIN_OUTSIDE_S, SPEED_MAX_KMH, TS_TOLERANCE_S
source: reference_data.yaml (FAIRRYDE, D, with plausible ranges)
note: Rated separately as parameters (credibility_principle) and tested case by case by the sensitivity test (decisive_definition clause 2); listed under CW-F04B in v0.2.

element: FairRyde's presence logic: the outlier, data-error, approach and window-edge rules and the values LEFT, SPARSE, CONSISTENT, UNKNOWN and GPS_AMBIGUOUS (moved from CW-F04 and shared with CW-R06's outlier step; GPS_AMBIGUOUS covers both window edges since check round 2)
source: FAIRRYDE (open items D18, D24, D26)
note: Split out of CW-F04 by FX4.

element: F-GPS-LOGIC: true when the logic, not the pings alone, makes the driver count as arrived and present (a ping set aside that could change the presence, in the window, or the arrival, one that would otherwise have been CW-R06's moment ping; an outside ping in the window not counted as leaving; an arrival confirmed only by a later ping, CW-F03B; SPARSE; GPS_AMBIGUOUS)
source: FAIRRYDE (FX4, step A3)
note: Feeds DT-CW-NOSHOW input gps_logic_decides (rows R8 and R11).

element: A fee upheld while F-GPS-LOGIC is true, or would be true with a CW-F04B parameter at an end of its plausible range, needs human approval (tier APPROVE), never AUTO: no-show fees through rows R9 and R11 (D, clauses 2 and 3), waiting fees through AUTH-02 trigger 12
source: FAIRRYDE-DECISIONS (Jasper, open item D29, 2026-10-11)
note: Implements D29; waiting fees have no decision table (D31), so the rule text and AUTH-02 carry it.

element: The cancellation and waiting policy applies to all service types except RydeTAXI
source: RYDE-4407761313305 (rider article, edited 2024-03-18): 'Cancellation Policy applies to all Service Types * in the Ryde app and is executed on a service level, not driver level.' and '*All services except RydeTAXI'
note: Ryde's own words; older than 12 months, so B.

element: A RydeTAXI cancellation-fee dispute has no written rule and is escalated
source: GEN-R07 (policy gap, rated D on its own card)
note: Pointer to GEN-R07, which carries its own label; the only outcome is escalation (tier HUMAN), so it never lets a case be decided automatically. Unlike FC-R00, the exclusion itself is Ryde's text.

element: An arrival indication is valid only if GPS shows the driver at the pick-up location
source: RYDE-4407754403353 (rider article, edited 2026-02-26): 'Drivers are only allowed to indicate arrival and impose the Waiting Time Fee only if he/she:' and 'Is at the pick-up location according to GPS data'
note: Read as covering the no-show fee by the META-04 resolution (interpretation), so B.

element: Otherwise no fee (FALSE: no GPS confirmation from the arrival to the cancellation, with remaining pings)
source: RYDE-4407754403353: 'Otherwise, you will not be charged the $6.61 Waiting Time Fee if any of the above are not fulfilled.'
note: This clause is one side of the META-04 fee-name conflict, so it cannot count toward A.

element: Confirmed at the arrival by the platform's own recorded GPS arrival check
source: ORG-DISP002: 'Driver GPS within 10m of pickup point. Speed 0 km/h. Auto-arrival confirmed.'
note: Organizer data.

element: Confirmed at the arrival by the moment ping (the last remaining ping from PING_MAX_GAP_S before to TS_TOLERANCE_S after the arrival) inside ARRIVAL_GEOFENCE_M
source: RYDE-4407754403353 ('according to GPS data', read at the moment of the indication); look-back, tolerance and radius are FAIRRYDE parameters (D)
note: Reading Ryde's GPS condition at the moment of the indication; the parameters are rated separately and tested by the sensitivity test.

element: GPS outliers are set aside before the check
source: FAIRRYDE (CW-F04B, open item D24)
note: Delegated to CW-F04B: when a set-aside ping would otherwise have been CW-R06's moment ping (or lies in the window), F-GPS-LOGIC is true and an upheld fee falls in row R11 (D). Setting aside removes evidence of absence, so a FALSE found after it is also FALSE on the pings alone, except a data error (gate G1, approval).

element: TRUE with ARRIVAL_UNCONFIRMED: confirmed only by a later ping
source: FAIRRYDE (CW-F03B, open item D26)
note: Delegated to CW-F03B (D): F-GPS-LOGIC is true (row R11 for an upheld fee); a short-wait waiver (R6, A) that rests on the moved start is caught by CW-F03B's start test, not by the row rating.

source: GEN-R02, DQ-01 (FAIRRYDE, D)
note: Row R2 is rated D.

source: GEN-R01 (D)
note: Row R3 is rated D.

source: IND-BENCHMARK-NOTES (research note 02: 'A late driver forfeits the fee almost everywhere: Grab (ETA plus 3 minutes), Gojek (ETA plus 5 minutes), Bolt ..., DiDi ..., Lyft scheduled ...')
note: Other platforms' practice; Ryde publishes no such rule.

element: A driver not moving toward the pick-up point makes it waivable (a driver already waiting at the pick-up counts as moving; for an advance booking, only a driver who could no longer arrive by the assignment ETA plus the grace)
source: FAIRRYDE (no local source: the round 1 reviewer found it on Grab's page, but research note 02 does not carry it)
note: Unsourced in the KB, so FairRyde's until a source is added (open item, A3). Since A4 the advance-booking ETA is a counted D element too, so sources for both would make the rule C again.

element: 'Assignment ETA' for an advance booking

element: Parameter DRIVER_LATE_GRACE_S

source: RYDE-30741244296217 (same); RYDE-360004075214 (RydeX article, edited 2024-10-08): 'All fares are fixed at the time of booking but does not include toll charges such as ERP.'
note: Same conflict; driver pages describe earnings by distance and time (META-04).

source: RYDE-50798691815449 (rider article, edited 2025-10-09): 'Once the driver accepts, your trip fare will be recalculated, and your route will be updated to the new destination'; RYDE-51399796192921 (2025-10-10): 'If the driver accepts your edit destination request, a $3.00 add/edit destination fee will apply.'
note: A3 adds the recalculation quote (the cited fee article does not say the fare is recalculated).

source: RYDE-34883561600025 (driver article): 'You will receive a notification or a request pop up on your Ryde Driver app when riders request to change the drop-off and/or add an additional drop-off stop.'; RYDE-51399674412441 (rider article): 'The rider can add another destination, leading to a map confirmation (for multiple stops).', 'New destination and fare confirmation will be displayed.'
note: A4 (FX7): the two articles differ in date and rollout status, so B; the rider article's next step carries the fare confirmation (check round 2).

source: LTA-PDVL-OFFENCES (PDVL offense list as at 1 Apr 2023): 'Failing, without reasonable cause, to proceed to destination named by a passenger by shortest and most direct route'
